method.before: Prior infallible Arrow integer-to-Decimal cast optimization with the same optional Spark fixes.
method.after: Same runtime plus the unchanged arrow-integer-decimal-reuse.patch.
method.retention: A prior SQL CAST(id AS DECIMAL(38,6)) output is retained while a later query streams. Drop the earlier stream before timing. batch holds 8192 rows; all holds 1048576; released drops a batch on another Rust thread before warmup.
method.ownership_probe: A separate 8192-row BIGINT to Decimal128(38,6) cast tests Buffer::into_mutable outside timing. This diagnostic allocation can affect allocator layout.
method.sql_timing: 12 processes per variant/mode/target and 4 per variant/mode/control, total 224. ABBA variants with rotating mode and case order. Median of 9 samples after 2 warmups, 1048576 rows, batch8192, one partition, CPU2. FIFO perf counters cover execution only; retained output checks and planning are excluded.
method.high_fault_group: More than 1000 page faults across 9 target executions. Observed slow processes have 18464, ordinary fallback fast processes 48-49, and reuse 16-17. This groups samples, not a statistical frequency estimate.
method.tracing: Eight fixed additional processes under strace; timing excluded. No slow sample reproduced, so no direct slow-mode syscall sequence is established by these traces.

source_audit.scope: Read-only audit of direct mutable conversion and mutable arithmetic call sites in the current reader, pinned DataFusion 54.1.0, its local dependency patches, Sail and Arrow 58.4.0. This does not cover arbitrary external consumers or future dependency versions.
source_audit.conclusion: No current SQL Decimal consumer was identified that gains an additional mutable-conversion copy from this owner. The public into_mutable/into_vec limitation remains. Retained output disables the global reuse slot until its last reference drops.

sources.finding: Buffer::into_mutable and into_vec reject custom deallocation; this is a real public Arrow ownership limitation.
convert_to_state uses binary_mut on its freshly allocated initial_state; the input values are only the borrowed right operand.
Mutable builders consume UInt64/UInt32 join indices, not Decimal value buffers.
into_data().into_builder() changes ArrayData null-mask metadata; it does not request mutable value allocation.
Nested NULL mask repair rebuilds ArrayData metadata, retaining value buffers.
Numeric operations use borrowed unary/try_unary/binary/try_binary kernels, rather than consuming the input through mutable kernels.
The currently patched round_columnar uses borrowed array traversal kernels.
scatter_updates reads base/update ArrayData into a newly allocated MutableArrayData; it does not reclaim the input value buffer.
Dictionary casts rebuild ArrayData metadata from cast integer keys and attach the cast values. They do not reclaim mutable Decimal value buffers.

Holding all batches also disables reuse even though 0/24 slow candidate processes were sampled. That observation cannot establish absence of slow allocation.
No audited current SQL Decimal consumer acquires an additional mutable-conversion copy; public into_mutable/into_vec limitations remain for external consumers.
The optional patch is not a general fix and is not promoted to default. Do not increase slot count without evaluating retained outputs and contention.
limitations: Same Linux/glibc host and selected batch/query sizes; no universal performance guarantee.
Later query streams rather than collecting its output. No Python C Stream or arbitrary concurrent-session validation in this slice.
Eight diagnostic traces missed the slow mode. The untraced fault signature matches prior evidence but does not directly prove the same syscall sequence.
Small process counts do not establish changes in the probability of slow allocation.
